traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.25, 0.22, 0.2], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Avicennia germinans (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.7 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 33 records in 9 sources); trunks 0.68, branches 0.66. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an evergreen tree of tropical and subtropical coasts, 5 to 10 m tall, with dark, scaly bark and narrow leaves grey-felted beneath, whose shallow roots send up hundreds of pencil-like breathing roots through the mud round it. Each bloom card stands for one of its cymes, 2 cm to 6 cm long as the species states, now that Acanthaceae's flowers are mostly in cymes (bloom_size 0.04, was 0.015, a single flower's size). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 5 m at 20 years and 8 m at 50. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: grey-green leaves, very dark bark. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): dark brown bark in irregular flat scales; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four white petals spreading from a short tube, four sepals, four stamens and a superior pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Acanthaceae and Avicennia by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
